title: Minimum Size Subarray Sum
summary: Given an array of positive integers, find the shortest subarray whose sum is at least a specified target.
statement: Given an array of positive integers, find the shortest subarray whose sum is at least a specified target. If no such subarray exists, return 0.
constraints: 1 ≤ target ≤ 10^9. nums contains 1–100000 POSITIVE integers, each at most 10000.
Return the shortest nonempty contiguous subarray length whose sum is at least target, or 0 if none exists. Do not reorder or skip intervening values.
hints: Positive values make the window sum increase when extending right and decrease when removing left.
Expand until the sum qualifies, then shrink repeatedly while it still qualifies.
Add each right value; while sum≥target, record the width and remove the left value. Return zero if no qualifying width was found.
The condition is at least the target, not exactly equal. Positivity is what makes the two-pointer reasoning valid.
editorial: For each right boundary, shrink until the remaining window no longer qualifies, checking every candidate width on the way. Each index enters and leaves once, so the total work is linear. The independent oracle enumerates each possible left boundary and directly accumulates rightward sums. Unlike existing exact-sum or maximum-length exercises, this asks for a minimum width with an inequality and guaranteed positive input.

tests.explanation: The contiguous final pair [4,3] sums to 7 and has length 2; no single value reaches 7.
A single 4 reaches the target, so the minimum length is 1.
